summary: Around 1900 a 50-foot wood lookout in Walnut Valley, NJ was replaced in 1922 by the Catfish Tower; the site is gone, with rumored remains on the Appalachian Trail.

facts.design: 50-foot wood tower built in Walnut Valley
facts.status_note: Register says the tower was replaced by the Catfish Tower in 1922; rumored pieces of cable and wood lie along the Appalachian Trail where it stood
facts.agency: National Park Service (administers the site, per the register)

visit.trail_note: Register says rumored pieces of cable and wood lie along the Appalachian Trail where the tower stood; no source describes the site today

events.note: Register says 'Around 1900' a 50-foot wood tower was built in Walnut Valley by local citizens
Replaced by the Catfish Tower, built 1922 by the State of New Jersey, several miles north along the ridgetop; Willhite describes it as a 60-foot Aermotor LS-40
Registered February 19, 2019 as FFLOS US 1740, NJ 7; nominated by Bob Spear

evidence.supports: built around 1900 as a 50-foot wood tower in Walnut Valley by local citizens
evidence.quote: Around 1900, this 50-foot wood tower was built in Walnut Valley by the citizens of the area.

evidence.supports: tower was meant to view Pennsylvania to the west and New Jersey farmland
evidence.quote: It was constructed for viewing the panorama of Pennsylvania to the west and the New Jersey farmlands.

evidence.supports: locals used it for Sunday excursions and picnics first; later fire wardens scouted for wildfires
evidence.quote: The tower was used by locals for Sunday excursions and picnics at first, and later by fire wardens to scout for wildfires.

evidence.supports: replaced in 1922 by the Catfish Tower built by the State of New Jersey, several miles north along the ridgetop
evidence.quote: It was later replaced by the Catfish Tower, built in 1922 by the State of New Jersey, several miles north along the ridgetop.

evidence.supports: rumored pieces of cable and wood lie along the Appalachian Trail where the tower stood
evidence.quote: There are rumored to be pieces of cable and wood from the old tower along the Appalachian Trail where it once stood.

evidence.supports: site lies within the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area
evidence.quote: Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area

evidence.supports: site administered by the National Park Service
registered February 19, 2019, nominated by Bob Spear
the state built a 60-foot Aermotor LS-40 tower near Catfish Pond in 1922
evidence.quote: In 1922, the state department of conservation and development built this 60 foot Aermotor LS-40 tower near Catfish Pond

evidence.supports: Willhite says a wooden tower stood at the Catfish location before 1922
evidence.quote: Prior to 1922, there was a wooden tower at this location.

evidence.supports: Catfish Tower is a standing lookout
Catfish Tower is staffed during moderate to high fire danger
evidence.quote: The tower is staffed during times of moderate to high fire danger.

resolved_conflicts.field: location of the earlier wooden tower
resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register places the 1900 wood tower in Walnut Valley, several miles south of Catfish; Willhite says a wooden tower stood at the Catfish site before 1922. Story reports both and does not decide whether they are the same tower.

sources.title: List of New Jersey Forest Fire Service fire towers

notes_for_editor: Brief's access 'unknown' not carried into facts: no source states access for this site, and NRA status alone would not establish public access, so story says only that the register places it in the NRA. Earlier wooden tower location conflicts between register (Walnut Valley) and Willhite (Catfish site); not resolved. Catfish elevation differs (Willhite 1,560 ft, Wikipedia 1,555 ft); not used in story. No dated staffing or fire events found in sources, so none are recorded. Wikipedia used only for the Catfish height. Second search returned nothing further on the Walnut Valley tower.
